Allow closure to finish, then make a short vertical test lift to check charger retention in RGB.

Continue the above-table turn and translate toward the far end of the charger for a grasp that allows upright insertion.

Lower toward the rear grasp height while completing yaw alignment, maintaining the same elbow-up branch.
Approach final rear-grasp height and align closer to the charger axis. Monitor wrist range and open-jaw clearance.
Fine-align rear approach from wrist RGB. Small increments near the wrist's current range; keep jaws open until the body is centered.
Yaw reached a joint wrap boundary; stop that turn and use small translations to center the rear grasp without changing branch.
Center the rear portion of the charger between the jaws and close. Small yaw mismatch remains, so verify capture before moving farther.
Complete closure and test a short upward retreat. Confirm the charger moves with the left jaws before orienting its pins downward.
Charger appears retained. Lift clear and start tipping its pins downward around the body-width axis, staying within continuous left-arm configuration.
Carry the retained charger toward the strip while progressively tipping the pins down; keep clearance and monitor the near-limit wrist joint.
Move toward the central socket, continue upright tipping, and start matching the pin separation direction to the strip's long axis.
Maintain charger retention while rotating toward upright; translate the wrist to compensate for the changing charger offset above the strip.
Refine the charger’s upright orientation from wrist silhouette and compensate its held offset while approaching the central socket.
Complete most of the remaining upright correction and socket yaw alignment. Keep charger elevated before attempting insertion.
Pins are approximately vertical. Move the held charger toward the central socket while lowering partway, using the next wrist view to refine socket alignment.
Keep the approximately upright, yaw-aligned charger steady and make a smaller approach toward the socket. Socket visibility is partly occluded by the held body.
The strip is entering the wrist view above the pins. Lower slowly without changing orientation to reveal the target holes and check alignment before seating.
Pins appear offset from the central socket's outer straight slots. Lift slightly out of contact and shift laterally to align the pair before another gentle descent.
Charger has visibly left the jaws during alignment. Stop insertion, open and retreat slightly while observing where it settles for recovery.
Keep clear of the strip and observe the displaced charger as it settles; no further insertion motion without a confirmed grasp.
Charger settled farther back on the left. Begin a cautious open-gripper recovery approach, reorienting toward it while preserving elbow-up continuity and reach margin.
Continue the left-side recovery approach at clearance height. The charger is distant; assess reach from the evolving elbow-up configuration rather than extending fully.
Advance toward the displaced charger with an open, forward-reaching gripper. Reduce downward tilt to improve reach while retaining elbow-up continuity.
Continue approaching the far-left charger, maintaining a shallow downward reach and open jaws. Will stop or replan if continuity or reach becomes constrained.
Advance along the charger approach line with fixed orientation, keeping the motion incremental and monitoring elbow-up reach.
Approach more slowly and roll the open jaws toward a level side grasp, preserving the forward direction and configuration continuity.
Advance incrementally toward the settled charger while leveling the jaw closing direction. Stop and replan if the far reach approaches a continuity limit.

Use smaller increments after the reach interruption. Level the open jaws while moving only a short distance toward the charger; maintain the selected elbow-up branch.
Forward reach is constrained. Retract slightly and aim the open fingers toward the charger without extending farther; reassess clearance and capture geometry.
The charger is beyond a comfortable direct grasp. Retreat from the reach limit and return toward the strip to consider a recovery that does not fully extend the arm.
Retreat command was rejected without movement. Replan with much smaller steps away from the reach boundary while keeping open jaws and elbow-up continuity.
Return to the nearer left workspace and turn the open gripper downward above the power strip, maintaining reach margin.
Move above the reachable power strip with open jaws and a downward grasp orientation. The charger remains beyond the previous comfortable reach.
Continue above the strip's right end, completing a downward grasp orientation. Keep both arms uncrossed and the left elbow on its current branch.
Align the open jaws over the reachable end of the strip, using a vertical approach and small orientation corrections.

Finish closing and make a short vertical test lift of the strip. Check RGB retention before carrying or using it for recovery.
Strip appears retained in the test lift. Raise it clear and begin turning its free end toward the distant charger, avoiding table contact.
Carry the retained strip toward the left-side charger at clearance height, turning its free end forward while keeping a bent elbow.
Continue positioning the strip's free end toward the charger, lowering only partway while preserving tabletop clearance and continuous elbow-up motion.
Angle the retained strip to extend its free end toward the charger while lowering gradually. Maintain clearance and a bent elbow; no sweeping contact yet.
Advance the strip's free end toward the displaced charger with fixed orientation, lowering slightly while monitoring reach and tabletop clearance.
Previous approach executed zero steps. Replan with smaller forward increments and a lower wrist height, checking that the strip remains retained and clear of the table.
Tracking residual and strip motion suggest tabletop contact. Back away and lift slightly, keeping the grip closed and avoiding further extension.
Retreat was rejected without execution. Use millimeter-scale withdrawal from the latest measured pose to restore reach margin and clear contact.
Withdraw to a comfortable reach and level the strip for a controlled placement. A different end-on grasp is needed to extend the tool without stretching the arm.
Place the leveled strip on the table, release it, and withdraw open jaws. Confirm its settled position for an end-on regrasp.
Withdraw clear of the released strip and turn the open gripper toward an end-on approach. Maintain elbow-up continuity and leave the strip undisturbed.
Continue toward a shallow end-on grasp of the strip, lowering behind its near end with open jaws while preserving clearance.
No previous steps executed. Reduce the combined wrist turn and descent by half and replan from the measured pose.
Move behind the near strip end while continuing the shallow approach orientation. Keep open jaws clear until the end is centered for the longitudinal grasp.
Continue descending behind the near strip end while flattening the gripper approach, leaving the strip undisturbed until the jaws align with its sides.
Continuity guard discarded the previous suffix. Replan from the measured pose using smaller combined descent and wrist-tilt increments.
Continue the low, end-on strip approach in small increments, centering the end between the open jaws while avoiding table contact.

Continue the open-gripper roll at clearance height, reducing wrist winding while keeping the approach axis and elbow-up branch continuous.
Continue rolling the open wrist clear of the table to obtain a level end-on grasp orientation, with no forward extension.
Continue the clearance-height wrist roll with open jaws; keep the arm position fixed and preserve configuration continuity.
Continue the open wrist roll to level the closing direction for a shallow end-on strip grasp. Hold position clear of the tabletop.
Finish leveling the open jaws and begin a slight descent toward the near strip end; confirm clearance before the final approach.

Lower the now-level open jaws to the strip's side height, with a small centering correction. Check for contact before closing.
Near strip end is centered at the jaw level. Lower eight millimeters and close for the longitudinal grasp, then verify retention with a short lift.
There is a small contact residual at the low grasp. Lift gently with the close target maintained, checking whether the strip rises with the jaws.
The strip did not visibly rise with the test lift. Reopen and advance the level jaws farther over its near end, slightly lower, for a deeper side grasp.
The strip is centered but the fingertips remain high. Tilt them down slightly without lowering the wrist housing, then close around the end's sides.
Allow the end-on grasp to close fully, then make a short test lift. Judge retention from whether the strip stays fixed relative to the fingers.

Advance the retained strip toward the charger at fixed height, stopping short of contact for another visual alignment check.
Move the strip tip alongside the charger with slight clearance, avoiding a straight push toward the table edge. Continue monitoring reach and retention.
Advance the retained strip tip along the charger’s side in smaller steps, leaving room to draw it away from the far edge rather than pushing it outward.
